channel.title: Oliver’s Lab — notes
channel.description: Notes from building a small cross-platform tool: scope, behaviour parity, naming, packaging and release checks. Written when a project ships, not to a schedule.

item.title: Why the launcher drives the app instead of the system proxy
item.description: A machine-wide proxy switch is one click and fails where you cannot see it. Scoping the same setting to a single process is more work to build and far easier to reason about — and it changes what a diagnostic is allowed to claim.

item.title: One behaviour, two builds
item.description: The Windows edition is not a port. What two native implementations share, what they cannot share, and how parity gets tested without an account, a display, or anyone to click.

item.title: Renaming a shipped app without breaking the upgrade path
item.description: A name is attached to six different things, and only some of them can change. What moved in 1.1.0, what stayed, and why the repository still carries the old name.

item.title: A version number is a build output
item.description: A version typed into four places is four versions. One file became the only source, and the release artefacts became things that can answer questions about themselves.
